paper: BVBRC-82 — Kim et al. 2020, Genome analysis of Bacteroides sp. CACC 737 (J Anim Sci Technol 62(6):952–955)
verdict_context: REPLICATED at the structural/deposit level; questions below are truly open — not answered by REPORT.md.

open_questions.q: Do the raw PacBio RS II + Illumina HiSeq reads (BioProject PRJNA647194) reassemble to the same complete circular chromosome + six plasmids, or is the deposited assembly authors'-pipeline-dependent?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §6 explicitly states 'Did not fetch SRA raw reads to verify PacBio+Illumina platform mix (BioProject PRJNA647194 exists but wasn't pulled). This is why C7 is UNRESOLVED, not FAILED.' Every quantitative claim we reproduced was pulled from the same GenBank deposit the authors submitted — so what we verified is provenance, not de novo assembly. The BV-BRC assigned workflow was 'PlasmidFinder via Similar Genome Finder + Genome Assembly (Unicycler/SPAdes),' and the assembly leg was never run.
next_steps: esearch/efetch SRA runs under PRJNA647194; log run IDs and platform metadata to confirm the paper's PacBio RS II + Illumina HiSeq mix (settles C7 directly).
Run Unicycler in hybrid mode (long PacBio + short Illumina) on uicgpu; or Flye + Pilon-polish as a cross-check.
Compare resulting contig set to the seven CP059406–CP059412 accessions: number of circular replicons, per-replicon length within tolerance, GC to two decimals, and any structural rearrangements.

open_questions.q: Are the six 'cryptic plasmids' truly six independent replicons, or does the ~99%-identity, 7–8 kb backbone shared across most plasmid pairs reflect assembly-collapse of a smaller number of true units?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §4d reports 'extensive shared regions of ~99% identity spanning 7–8 kb between most plasmid pairs' from all-vs-all plasmid BLAST, interpreted as the 'cryptic Bacteroides plasmid family' rep/mob backbone. But the same signature is also consistent with an assembler splitting one physical plasmid into multiple contigs, or two plasmids being nearly identical copies. Nothing in the run resolves that ambiguity.
next_steps: Map raw PacBio long reads back to each plasmid; long reads that span the full plasmid unambiguously prove independent circular topology and per-plasmid coverage.
Compute per-plasmid read depth from Illumina remap; markedly non-integer coverage ratios (e.g. 2:1) between plasmids would suggest copy-number differences or misassembly.
Confirm each plasmid closure (matching start/end contig ends per GenBank 'topology=circular') by inspecting overlap junctions in the original assembly graph.

open_questions.q: Does CACC 737 actually carry '2 confirmed + 1 questionable' CRISPR array — and Type II CAS specifically — when a locus-level tool (CRISPR-Cas web server, CRISPRCasFinder, or CRISPRDetect) is run against the chromosome?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §4c reports 44 chromosome CDS matching CRISPR|Cas as a product-name regex, and §5 marks C6 as CONSISTENT with the note 'exact count of two regions not independently confirmed.' §6 states explicitly 'Did not run the CRISPR web server. We confirmed CRISPR/Cas-annotated CDSs on the chromosome; the 2 confirmed + 1 questionable locus count is a caller-specific output and would require running the specific tool.' Cas subtype (Type II) is also an unverified caller-level attribution — Bacteroides more commonly carry Type I-B/I-C than Type II.
next_steps: Run CRISPRCasFinder (Docker image is public) against CP059408; enumerate arrays, repeat consensus, spacer count, evidence level (1–4), and confirmed vs questionable calls.
Cross-check with CRISPRDetect and/or the current CRISPR-Cas++ web server; compare array coordinates.
Type the Cas cassette (Cas9 signature = Type II; Cas3 = Type I; Cas13 = Type VI) from the flanking Cas gene set to confirm or refute the Type II assignment.

open_questions.q: Do the four chromosomal 16S paralogs give the same identity to *B. uniformis* type strain, and does the 97.5%-vs-97.83% offset from the paper survive under a second aligner (BLASTN, EMBOSS needle) with characterized parameters?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §4b explicitly compares one 16S copy (the first) against NR_112945.1 using Biopython pairwise2.align.globalms(2,-1,-2,-0.5) and reports 97.83% vs paper 97.5%, calling the 0.33 pp gap 'well within alignment-algorithm noise.' The four paralogs are stated to be 1,534 bp each, but per-paralog identity is not reported; the paper's aligner is not stated; and no second-aligner comparison was run. Both values sit comfortably below the 98.6% novel-species threshold, so the qualitative verdict is robust — but the quantitative offset is not actually characterized.
next_steps: Extract all four 16S paralogs from CP059408; report per-paralog identity to NR_112945.1 (and, separately, to the ATCC 8492ᵀ record if a distinct accession exists).
Re-align with BLASTN (megablast + blastn task) and EMBOSS needle at published Bacteroidota 16S parameters; report identity range across aligners.
If the paper's Materials & Methods or supplement names the aligner, replicate under those exact parameters.

open_questions.q: Does an independent re-annotation (Prokka, Bakta, or a fresh RAST run) reproduce the paper's 3,938-CDS total, and if so, which functional categories (hypotheticals, short ORFs, overlapping calls) explain the 3,682 vs 3,938 gap and the ~50% CDS shortfalls on small plasmids (e.g. CP059407: 12 vs 25; CP059410: 13 vs 35)?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §4a shows CDS 3,682 (ours, from PGAP-only GenBank) vs 3,938 (paper, PGAP+RAST merged). §5 labels C4 as CONSISTENT with 'typical PGAP vs RAST annotation differences.' §6 states 'Did not re-run PGAP+RAST. The 3,682-vs-3,938 CDS delta is explained by pipeline-combination differences, but a true re-annotation on uicgpu (Prokka + RAST) would tighten this.' The plasmid-level deltas — half of the paper's CDS on some 20–30 kb plasmids — are absorbed into the same narrative without being quantified.
next_steps: Run Prokka and Bakta (both current) on CP059406–CP059412 on uicgpu; diff CDS sets against the deposited PGAP annotation.
Submit CP059408 to RAST and re-merge with PGAP by the same rule the paper implies; check whether merged total lands near 3,938.

For each plasmid, enumerate CDS calls unique to each pipeline by length class and category (hypothetical, mobile-element, replication) to attribute the gap to concrete calling differences rather than an unquantified 'pipeline noise' story.
